title: Closed-fibre section vanishing gives maximal-ideal divisibility
statement: Let A be a valuation domain with maximal ideal m. Let f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}(A) be proper, flat and of finite presentation [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], let L be an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module], and suppose that X\times_A\operatorname{Spec}(A/m) is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Let s\in\Gamma(X,L). The fibre at the unique closed point of Spec A is integral; moreover, if s restricts to zero on that fibre, with restriction given by the unit of the tensor-pullback adjunction [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction], then there are \pi\in m and t\in\Gamma(X,L) with \pi t=s. Scalars act through A=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}(A),\mathcal O)\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X). The case that A is a field is included, and \pi is allowed to be zero.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma lemma-triviality-generic-fibre-valuation-ring, Tag 0EX8, general-case proof

proof.text: The Spec residue-field identification identifies the residue field at the closed point with the residue field of the local ring A, namely A/m; localization at its maximal ideal does not change A because the elements inverted are already units. The point map commutes with this isomorphism. Pull back this isomorphism along f. It transports the hypothesis of integral quotient fibre to the scheme-theoretic fibre and identifies section restrictions through the tensor-pullback adjunction.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma lemma-triviality-generic-fibre-valuation-ring, Tag 0EX8, general-case proof

proof.text: If A is a field, the quotient point map and the closed-fibre inclusion are isomorphisms. Vanishing of the restricted section implies s=0, so pi=0 and t=0 give the desired equality.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma lemma-triviality-generic-fibre-valuation-ring, Tag 0EX8, general-case proof

proof.text: Otherwise apply the closed-fibre section-vanishing lemma to the quotient fibre, using properness for quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. It supplies nonzero pi in m and vanishing on X times Spec(A/(pi)).

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma lemma-triviality-generic-fibre-valuation-ring, Tag 0EX8, general-case proof

proof.text: The closed-immersion unit-quotient theorem identifies the kernel of restriction modulo pi with (pi)L. Flatness of X/A and local freeness of L make multiplication by nonzero pi injective on L, so multiplication identifies L with this kernel. The vanishing hypothesis puts s in the kernel. On a cover it has lifts t; any two local lifts coincide on overlaps by injectivity and therefore glue to a global t with pi t=s. This uses no basis hypothesis.

mathlib_searches.query: A section of an invertible sheaf vanishing on the closed fibre over a valuation ring is divisible by an element of the maximal ideal
An invertible module section which restricts to zero modulo a nonzero scalar is divisible by that scalar on a scheme flat over a domain

lean.statement:
theorem closed_fibre_vanishing_is_divisible
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [ValuationRing A]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of A))
    [IsProper f] [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (L : X.Modules) [L.IsInvertible]
    (hX₀ : IsIntegral (Limits.pullback f (Spec.map
      (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A))))))
    (s : Γ(L, ⊤)) :
    IsIntegral (f.fiber (IsLocalRing.closedPoint A)) ∧
      (((Classical.choose (exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction
        (f.fiberι (IsLocalRing.closedPoint A)))).unit.app L).val.app (op ⊤) s = 0 →
        ∃ π : A, π ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A ∧ ∃ t : Γ(L, ⊤),
          ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of A)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom π • t = s)
